title: Content brief from a keyword export
prompt:
You are the SEO lead for Fernhollow Tea, an online loose-leaf tea shop. The content lead has room for one new article this month and wants a content brief a writer can start from. You are supplied the keyword export from the SEO tool, the list of pages the site already has, and the outlines of two competing articles. Every figure you cite must come from the supplied files.

Use these definitions exactly:
- A keyword already belongs to an existing page when its `current_rank` is 10 or better. Those keywords are not targets for a new article.
- A qualifying keyword has informational intent, a difficulty of 45 or lower, and is not one the site already ranks in the top 10 for.
- The target topic is the `topic` whose qualifying keywords have the highest combined `monthly_searches`.
- The primary keyword is the qualifying keyword in the target topic with the most monthly searches.

Write the brief: the target topic and why it wins on the numbers; the primary keyword and the secondary keywords; the search intent and the format that serves it; a working title and a meta description; an outline of H2 sections that covers what the qualifying keywords show people asking; what this article will cover that neither competing outline does; and at least two existing pages it should link to, by URL.

End the brief with an answer block in exactly this format, one line per answer. Each line is the label, a colon, and the number alone: no words, no working and no second number. A currency sign, thousands separators and a percent sign are fine.

A1: <how many keywords in the export the site already ranks in the top 10 for>
A2: <how many qualifying keywords the target topic has>
A3: <combined monthly searches of the target topic's qualifying keywords>
A4: <monthly searches of the primary keyword>
A5: <combined monthly searches of the keywords the site already ranks in the top 10 for>

This is a planning document for internal review. Do not fetch external data, and do not estimate traffic the export does not show.

completion.check: The response ends with the required answer block and all 5 labeled answers A1-A5 are present, each on its own line with the number alone.
A1 states how many keywords in the export the site already ranks in the top 10 for; full credit for the exact figure, zero credit 3 or more off.
A2 states how many qualifying keywords the target topic has; full credit for the exact figure, zero credit 3 or more off.
A3 states the combined monthly searches of the target topic's qualifying keywords; full credit within 0.5%, zero credit beyond 25% off.
A4 states the monthly searches of the primary keyword; full credit within 0.5%, zero credit beyond 25% off.
A5 states the combined monthly searches of the keywords the site already ranks in the top 10 for; full credit within 0.5%, zero credit beyond 25% off.

The brief contains all of: a named target topic, a primary keyword and secondary keywords, a statement of search intent, a working title and a meta description, an outline of H2 sections, and existing pages to link to. One missing element fails.

skill_adherence.check: The brief targets the cold brew tea topic and names it as the target. Targeting any other topic fails.
The primary keyword is 'how to cold brew tea'. Any other primary keyword fails.

No keyword the site already ranks in the top 10 for (best green tea, green tea caffeine, matcha caffeine, how to store loose leaf tea, does tea expire, does cold brew tea go bad) is listed as a primary or secondary keyword of the new article. Linking to the pages that rank for them is fine; listing one of them as a target fails.
The brief lists at least two internal URLs to link to, and every internal URL it lists appears in the supplied page list. Fewer than two, or any URL that is not in the list, fails.

Every search volume, difficulty score and ranking position presented as a fact matches the keyword export, and the brief gives no traffic, click or revenue forecast as if it were data. Explicitly labelled assumptions are not data.

best_practices.check: The brief states that the search intent is informational and proposes an explanatory how-to article. It fails if no intent is stated, or if the proposed format is a product roundup, buying guide or category page.
The outline has a section on the tea-to-water ratio and a section on how long to steep, the two highest-volume qualifying questions after the primary keyword. Missing either fails.

The brief names at least one subtopic that the keyword export shows demand for and that neither competing outline covers (the caffeine content of cold brew tea, or cold-brewing with tea bags) and includes it in the outline. Naming as the gap something one of the competitors already covers (ratio, steep time, equipment, storage, green tea, cold brew versus iced tea) fails.
